pr_title: roachtest: export tpce perf data to roachperf
pr_body: This changes the tpce/c=* tests to export TradeResult transaction latencies to a stats.json that is uploaded to roachperf. Fixes: #127035 Release note: none Epic: none ------------------ For the roachperf PR see: https://github.com/cockroachdb/roachperf/pull/168 Note the latency fluctuated so much because I only ran the workload for 1 minute to save time/money.

issue_context.title: roachtest: add tpc-e to roachperf
issue_context.body:
We run [TPC-E](https://github.com/cockroachlabs/tpc-e) nightly, but don't currently track its performance in roachperf. We should so that we can track performance over time and catch performance regressions.

Jira issue: CRDB-40248
comments: What metrics do we care about here? For reference, this is what the tests currently spit out for performance: Maybe just txn/s? But even then that seems like it would be way too much info for roachperf unless we want to aggregate it.

Let's go with throughput and latency of `TradeResult` [1],

> 6.6.8.4 The Measured Throughput is computed as the total number of Valid Trade-Result Transactions
within the Measurement Interval divided by the duration of the Measurement Interval in seconds.

[1] https://www.tpc.org/tpc_documents_current_versions/pdf/tpc-e_v1.14.0.pdf
TPC-E is an open-loop workload with a fixed rate of transactions, so throughput should be stable unless (average) latency tanks. Maybe we plot different percentiles of `TradeResult` latency?

review_comments: Should we mark this test spec with `Benchmark: true`? I know it's not strictly required for this to work, but it's confusing for a test not marked as benchmark to show up on roachperf.
